result:
Here's a complete picture:

---

**There is no single content-type dispatch router.** Hono exposes three independent body-parsing methods on `HonoRequest`, and the caller chooses which to invoke. The content-type header is only inspected inside `parseBody`.

### `c.req.parseBody()` — `src/utils/body.ts:94–111`

This is the only method that reads `Content-Type`. The dispatch at lines 103–108:

```
multipart/form-data              → parseFormData()   (calls request.formData())
application/x-www-form-urlencoded → parseFormData()  (same path)
anything else                    → returns {}
```

`parseBody` is **not** a general "parse whatever the body is" function — it only handles form payloads. JSON and text bodies will silently return `{}` if called through `parseBody`.

### `c.req.json()` — `src/request.ts:253–255`

No content-type check at all. It calls `this.#cachedBody('text')` (which reads `raw.text()`) then `JSON.parse()`s the result. It will throw a SyntaxError if the body isn't valid JSON; it won't reject based on the header.

### `c.req.text()` — `src/request.ts:269–271`

Same: just `this.#cachedBody('text')` → `raw.text()`. No content-type awareness.

### `c.req.arrayBuffer()` — `src/request.ts:285–287`

Same pattern: `this.#cachedBody('arrayBuffer')` → `raw.arrayBuffer()`.

### The caching layer — `src/request.ts:220–239`

`#cachedBody` de-duplicates reads: once any key is consumed it re-derives other formats from the cached result (e.g. JSON bodies can be re-read as text via `JSON.stringify` round-trip), so you can call `req.json()` and `req.text()` on the same request without consuming the stream twice.

**Summary:** The only content-type-aware dispatch is in `parseBody` at `src/utils/body.ts:103–108`, and it only distinguishes form payloads vs. everything-else. `json()` and `text()` are unconditional — they're caller-directed, not content-type-directed.
